newsitem.title: CANADA: Abitibi-Price rises as market likes merger.
newsitem.headline: Abitibi-Price rises as market likes merger.

text.p: Shares of Abitibi-Price Inc rose 0.50 to 23.60 on the Toronto Stock Exchange and 7/8 to 17-3/8 on the New York Stock Exchange Tuesday morning, showing market approval of the company's proposed merger with Stone-Consolidated Corp, analysts said.

Independent forest products sector analyst John Duncanson, said Abitibi-Price shares were up most likely on renewed interest in the stock by investors in the United States, where markets were closed on Monday.
On Friday, Abitibi-Price and Stone-Consolidated said they planned to merge in an all-stock swap.
"Most institutions in the United States are probably realizing that this is going to mean a great industry rationalization and consolidation," Duncanson said.
On Tuesday morning, Goldman Sachs said it had upgraded Abitibi-Price to market outperfrom from market perform.

The merger would create the world's largest newsprint maker by a wide margin, and expectations are that certain of the older mills among the 18 the merged company, Abitibi-Consolidated, would own might be sold, or some older and less efficient newsprint making machines might be taken off stream.
That would help tighten a newsprint market that has been plagued by high producer and consumer inventories and prices that are currently at a cyclical low of US$500 a metric ton.

On Tuesday, shares of Stone-Consolidated were up 0.30 to 23.65. Under the merger agreement, one share of Abitibi-Price would be exchanged for one share in Abitibi-Consolidated, while each common share of Stone-Consolidated would be exchanged for 1.0062 common shares of Abitibi-Consolidated.

Stone Container Corp, which owns 46.6 percent of Stone-Consolidated, would own about 25 percent of the merged company. On Tuesday morning, Stone Container's shares were down 1/8 to 12-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
